text:
marina: FYI I promoted Ivy-9B (int4) to a small canary this morning. seeing p99 tail latency up ~20% vs our 9B baseline for short-convo traces :grimacing:

marina: baseline p95 ok, spikes at p99 when batch>4 and on first requests after node cold start. also some OOM fallbacks logged.

sanjay: can reproduce locally with prod-sample replay. p99 spikes correlate with kv cache misses and big memcpy durations.

lucas: paste logs? want to check memcpy vs compute ratios.

marina: log excerpt:
```
[2026-03-21T09:14:22Z] worker-7 | req=xyz987 batch=6 max_new_tokens=64
[2026-03-21T09:14:22Z] worker-7 | kv_miss shard=2 slot_alloc=failed try=1
[2026-03-21T09:14:22Z] worker-7 | memcpy 32ms compute 15ms total_lat 112ms p99
[2026-03-21T09:14:22Z] worker-7 | OOM-fallback: reclaimed 96MB
```

marta: that smells like fragmentation + prefetch allocations. are we running the int4 prefetch path for Ivy?

marina: yes prefetch=enabled by default. i flipped prefetch off on node subset and saw immediate p99 drop ~11ms.

sanjay: interesting. for Ivy the kv chunk size was bumped to 1.5x to optimize throughput; prefetch may be reserving larger contiguous blocks which fragment. batching amplifies it.

lucas: propose two quick ablations on replay traffic: config X = prefetch=false, max_batch=4, slot_reserve_mb=128; config Y = prefetch=true, max_batch=3, warmup_reserve_mb=256 for 20s on cold start. run 45m each.

marina: launching X against group gamma now. deploy-bot: canary deploy started for route ivy-int4-ablation-20260321-X.

deploy-bot: node1 updated -> node2 updated -> canary live.

marta: please also lower kv_eviction_threshold to 0.65 for X, keep 0.75 for Y. should reduce transient evicts on X.

sanjay: config X snippet:
```
model: ivy-9b-int4
prefetch: false
batching:
  max_batch: 4
kv:
  slot_reserve_mb: 128
  eviction_threshold: 0.65
max_new_tokens_default: 64
```

sanjay: config Y snippet:
```
model: ivy-9b-int4
prefetch: true
batching:
  max_batch: 3
kv:
  warmup_slot_reserve_mb: 256
  warmup_duration_s: 20
  eviction_threshold: 0.75
max_new_tokens_default: 64
```

lucas: ok run plan. capture p50/p95/p99, memcpy histograms, OOM-fallback counts, and the tiny-qa eval set (EM/F1).

marina: X finished (45m). summary uploaded to /replay/runs/ivy/20260321/X_summary.json

marta: X results: p99 reduced 10-13ms on short-chat traces, OOM-fallbacks down 68%, memcpy tail reduced. small QA drop: em -0.6%.

marina: started Y now. deploy-bot: canary Y started for route ivy-int4-ablation-20260321-Y.

deploy-bot: canary Y complete (45m). Artifact at /replay/runs/ivy/20260321/Y_summary.json

lucas: Y results: p99 reduced 6-8ms, OOM-fallbacks down 40%, QA stable (no significant EM/F1 change). warmup path seems to blunt coldstart spikes but gives smaller steady-state gains.

sanjay: tradeoff summary: X = better latency + mem stability, slight QA regression. Y = safer quality, modest latency gains. hypothesis: prefetch=false reduces fragmentation but interacts with quantized kernel numerics causing token-drop in edge prompts.

marta: suggestion: for immediate canary set Y as default (prefetch on, small batch), and run a longer 24h experiment with X but increase max_new_tokens_default to 96 to see if QA recovers. also open a runtime ticket for memcpy kernel investigation.

lucas: creating ticket RI-2026-ivy-int4-memcpy-investigation with traces and memcpy histograms attached.

marina: rolling Y to canary route ivy-int4-canary-safe. updated model catalog notes with recommended defaults: max_batch=3, prefetch=on, kv_eviction=0.75, max_new_tokens_default=64, warmup_reserve=256MB for 20s. link to A/B artifacts. :white_check_mark:

marta: thanks. ping if 24h X-run shows any QA drift and we'll revert.

sanjay: good plan. follow-up tasks: (1) 24h X-run with max_new_tokens=96, (2) perf team to look at memcpy vectorized copy path, (3) bake warmup into onboarding template.

marina: noted, starting 24h X-run now on group delta. will report back. :rocket:
